extracted.intended_audience: prospective and current NIDDK trainees, applicants for NIDDK training/fellowship/K awards, mentors, and training program administrators
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance on eligibility, application, administration, and obligations for NIDDK training grants, individual fellowships, and K-series career development awards. Covers whom NIDDK funds, transfer/relocation rules, mentor responsibilities, stipend/payback obligations, and loan repayment rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Applicant initial self-assessment
rubrics_metrics.description: Start by answering the following questions, which would be posed to you if you contacted one of the NIDDK training program directors: Are you an M.D. or a Ph.D? How long ago did you get your degree? Do you want to do basic or clinical research? If clinical, will you be dealing with patients directly or indirectly? What research experience do you have? Where are you located? Are you planning on staying there? Do you have publications? Is your CV up to date? Where would you like to be, career-wise, 10 yrs from now?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use these questions to determine the appropriate career-stage pages and whether to contact a program director; they frame eligibility and fit for different awards.

rubrics_metrics.name: Citizenship/residency eligibility
rubrics_metrics.description: You must be a U.S. citizen or permanent resident to receive funding for a training grant, individual fellowship, or career development award, with the exception of the K99/R00.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: You may apply for an F32 or K award while you are in the process of becoming a permanent resident or citizen, if your institution allows it. R-series grants do not have this restriction.

rubrics_metrics.name: How to find a postdoctoral position
rubrics_metrics.description: You can find a postdoctoral position by doing a keyword search using the NIH RePORTer system to see who the NIDDK is currently supporting and contacting principal investigators directly; limit search by state and to 'research grants'.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If interested in intramural positions, consult the NIDDK Training and Employment page. Contact PIs to see if they will accept another postdoc.

rubrics_metrics.name: Types and forms of NIDDK training support
rubrics_metrics.description: NIDDK offers intramural and extramural funding opportunities; support can be in the form of a training grant (institution selects trainees) or individual fellowships/career development awards (applicants identify a sponsor/mentor and have their institution submit an application to NIH).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants for fellowships/career development awards must identify a sponsor/mentor and have their university or medical school submit the application on their behalf.

rubrics_metrics.name: Relocation/transfer approval conditions (moving with mentor)
rubrics_metrics.description: You may move with your mentor provided your project does not change substantially, the new institution will accept your grant, and the new institution can provide an environment, resources, and career development activities comparable to your current institution.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Contact your Research Training and Career Development program director prior to submitting paperwork to discuss the move and to be assured it will (or will not) be approved. Review NIDDK instructions for requesting relocation/transfer for F32 and K-series.

rubrics_metrics.name: Relocation/transfer conditions (staying when mentor leaves)
rubrics_metrics.description: If your mentor is moving but you want to stay, you may remain if you can identify a new mentor, your project does not change, and your department/division indicates it will still support you.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: You may keep your current mentor as a long-distance co-mentor. Discuss the change with the Research Training and Career Development program director, who approves or disapproves the request.

rubrics_metrics.name: Leave (maternity/other) and award continuation
rubrics_metrics.description: The NIH allows you to receive the same benefits as anyone employed by your institution; if local policy allows paid maternity leave, you may draw salary from your K award during that period. You may take unpaid leave with institutional and mentor concurrence if your project will still be viable after the leave.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Time away may be added to the end of your funding period (no-cost extension). Discuss leave with your program director who must approve or disapprove requests.

rubrics_metrics.name: T32 appointment citizenship and experience restrictions
rubrics_metrics.description: A candidate for any National Research Service Award position must be a U.S. citizen or permanent resident. Postdoctoral trainees with no clinical responsibilities and more than 5 years of postdoctoral research experience (stipend-level 6 or higher) must receive prior approval from NIDDK before being appointed to an NIDDK training grant.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Send the trainee's biosketch to your Research Training and Career Development program director for consideration. T32 is not intended to support advanced post-doctoral fellows.

rubrics_metrics.name: T32 predoctoral slot availability
rubrics_metrics.description: If you do not have approved pre-doctoral slots available in your T32, you may not appoint a pre-doctoral student.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Program directors must verify slot availability before appointments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Which K award to apply for (degree/research-type mapping)
rubrics_metrics.description: If you are an M.D. or hold a comparable clinical doctoral degree and are doing basic research, apply for a K08. If doing clinical research with direct patient interaction, apply for a K23. If you are a Ph.D. or a nonboard-eligible M.D., apply for a K01. If you are a nonbiomedically trained Ph.D moving into biomedical research, apply for a K25.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The NIDDK does not support the K02 award for more senior scientists. See the K awards overview for conditions of each award.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mentor expectations on a K award
rubrics_metrics.description: A K-award mentor advises a candidate on scientific and career issues and is an advocate at the institutional level; the mentor and department/institution must ensure the awardee has protected time and resources needed to complete the research project and career development plans.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The project should allow the candidate to distinguish his or her career from the mentor’s (cannot be one of the aims from the mentor’s R01). The awardee should be free to take the project if he or she leaves the institution.

rubrics_metrics.name: K award change-of-institution and international restriction
rubrics_metrics.description: An active K award can be transferred: the current institution must relinquish the award and the new institution must apply as a change-of-institution application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: NIDDK does not support K awards outside the United States; you cannot take a K award to a laboratory outside the U.S.

rubrics_metrics.name: New investigator status while holding a K award
rubrics_metrics.description: Holding a K award does not change your 'new investigator' status for R01 applications; the NIH does not consider K awards independent grants since you have a mentor.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: You are still a 'new investigator' when you apply for your first R01.

rubrics_metrics.name: Concurrent K and R01 funding: effort/salary rules
rubrics_metrics.description: Whether you can draw salary from both the K and R depends on how many years remain on your K award. If you are in the final 2 years of your K, you may keep both awards and draw a salary from both. If your salary is more than $100,000 and the K award does not equal a true 75% of your salary, NIH can reduce your effort on the K without reducing the award amount.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The total of your effort on the K and the R must not fall below 75%, with the K effort remaining at a minimum of 50%. This policy is in the NIH Grants Policy Statement (NIH GPS).

rubrics_metrics.name: K12 and individual K combined duration limit
rubrics_metrics.description: If you are currently funded by a K12 program, NIDDK will only award an individual K award for the number of years that will give you a total of 6 years of support on the K12 and the individual K combined.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Plan total career-development duration accordingly.

rubrics_metrics.name: PI/mentee change policy on K awards
rubrics_metrics.description: If an applicant on a K01 award is no longer available, the Mentor of the application may not change the Mentee; the PI of any K award cannot change.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: K awards bind the PI/mentee pairing in the funded application.

rubrics_metrics.name: Loan repayment eligibility while on a training grant
rubrics_metrics.description: You can apply for a loan repayment while on a training grant as long as at the time the loan repayment contract would be issued you have 2 remaining years of research time.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For new applications, loan repayment contracts are for 2 years, not 1. Example: appointed in July and applying in December, you should have 2 years of research training remaining as of July of the following year.

rubrics_metrics.name: Payback obligation definition
rubrics_metrics.description: Payback means you should stay on a postdoctoral training grant or individual postdoctoral fellowship, or any combination of the two, for 2 full years.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is the general meaning of payback for NRSA-related training.

rubrics_metrics.name: Which awards incur payback (predoctoral vs postdoctoral)
rubrics_metrics.description: Predoctoral support, limited to 5 years, does not incur a payback obligation. Every postdoctoral NRSA fellow (T32, F32, or any combination) incurs an obligation to 'pay back' the first 12 months of NRSA support; months 13 and beyond are the usual 'pay back'.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This policy is in place because studies show postdocs with 2+ years of research after degree are more likely to pursue research careers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consequences and remediation for not completing payback
rubrics_metrics.description: At appointment/activation you sign a payback agreement. If you do not complete 24 months of NRSA support, you must verify you are engaged in bona fide research or other specified activities for a minimum of 20 hours a week to complete your service obligation. If unwilling to complete the obligation, the government may expect monetary compensation with interest for the NRSA support received.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Be aware of the signed obligations and the alternatives (continuing research activity) to avoid financial penalties.

rubrics_metrics.name: NIDDK does not provide scholarships but supports predoctoral training
rubrics_metrics.description: NIDDK does not supply 'scholarships', but supports the training of predoctoral students on institutional training grants and via individual fellowships (F31, PA-11-112).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If seeking scholarship-style funding, note the distinction: support comes through training grants or fellowships, not scholarships administered by NIDDK.

rubrics_metrics.name: Master's degree tuition support policy
rubrics_metrics.description: NIDDK does not usually pay for a master's degree; NIDDK supports predoctoral training, not graduate work leading to a masters.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Exception: for a physician or Ph.D. supported by a grant (such as an F32 or K award) that would allow tuition payment for a master's degree.

rubrics_metrics.name: Stipend level progression rules
rubrics_metrics.description: NIH sets stipend levels beginning at the 0 level of experience (the year following completion of a doctoral degree). A trainee must complete a full year of postdoctoral training to receive the next higher stipend level.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: if a trainee has received 18 months of training, he/she would receive the level-one stipend and remain at that level the entire year; upon reappointment the individual would receive the level-two stipend.
